title: 600,000 People Pack Paris Streets to See Pope Leo!
summary:
Imagine a parade so big it fills an entire famous street. That's what happened in Paris on Saturday! More than 600,000 people signed up to see Pope Leo XIV. He rode through the city in his popemobile (a special vehicle with clear walls so everyone can see the Pope) along the Champs-Élysées, a wide avenue as long as 20 football fields. The parade was 2 kilometres long and ended at Place de la Concorde, a huge square in the middle of Paris.

Pope Leo is from America. He came to France for four days. On Friday, he visited Notre-Dame Cathedral, which was badly damaged by a fire in 2019 and has just been fixed up. He is the first pope to pray there since that fire.

Not everyone who came was Catholic. Some people came just to hear his message about peace and helping others. "It's not only about seeing the Pope," said Sylvane Le Goff, 68, who brought her grandchildren, ages 10 and 12. "It's about his message of peace and unity."

Some people in France think the Pope should not have held the mass at Place de la Concorde. They say that square belongs to the government, not the church. But for one day, it was filled with people of all backgrounds, celebrating together.
why_it_matters: A message about peace and unity can bring together hundreds of thousands of people who don't even share the same religion — just like one kind speech or act can bring a whole school together.

background_read: The Pope is the leader of the Catholic Church, a Christian church with more than a billion members around the world. He normally lives in Vatican City (a tiny country inside Rome, Italy).
Notre-Dame Cathedral is a very famous, very old church in Paris. A huge fire damaged it in 2019, and people from around the world gave money to help rebuild it.
A 'mass' is a Catholic religious service, and the Champs-Élysées is one of the most famous streets in the world — it is often used for parades and big celebrations.
Article_Structure: WHO: Pope Leo XIV (the Pope, who is from America), more than 600,000 people who signed up to see him, and visitors like Sylvane Le Goff, 68, who brought her grandchildren, ages 10 and 12.
WHAT: The Pope rode through Paris in his popemobile in a 2-kilometre parade, prayed at Notre-Dame Cathedral, and shared a message about peace and helping others.
WHERE: Paris, France — along the Champs-Élysées and ending at Place de la Concorde, plus a visit to Notre-Dame Cathedral.
WHY: He came to France for a four-day visit; he is the first pope to pray at Notre-Dame since the 2019 fire, and his message drew both Catholic and non-Catholic crowds.
